newsitem.title: USA: Chicago mayor says state move to hurt bond ratings.
newsitem.headline: Chicago mayor says state move to hurt bond ratings.

text.p: Chicago Mayor Richard Daley said Wednesday that he was concerned the Illinois House's passage Tuesday night of a bill allowing the state to take over a small city airport could impair the bond ratings of the city and other municipalities in the state.

Flanked by mayors of suburban communities and other business and civic leaders, Daley blasted Republican Gov. Jim Edgar for orchestrating a legislative takeover of Meigs Field, an airport on Chicago's downtown lakefront.
"What happened in Springfield yesterday was unpredicented," Daley said, referring to the bill's passage that was supported by the Republican majority.

Daley said the move raised concerns about bond ratings for the city and other municipalities that he warned may also find themselves on the wrong end of state legislation if their policies conflict with the wishes of state officials. In this case, Edgar wants to keep the airport, which the city shut down earlier this fall, operating, while Daley wants to turn it into a $27 million, bond-financed nature park.

"And if this bill becomes law, every local government in Illinois should be concerned. Because if a local government disagrees with the state government about zoning or land use, they might mandate change in Springfield," Daley said.
Walter Knorr, Chicago's chief financial officer, said the rating agencies have the matter "on the radar screen."
"Time will tell tell if it will evolve into a true credit concern," he said.
Rating analysts said this week they were currently viewing the matter as a single incident.
"One action does not necessarily make a trend," said Jeff Panger, a director at Standard & Poor's Corp.
Harvey Zachem, a analyst at Moody's Investors Service, said that the matter could become a concern for home-rule municipalities that stand to lose some of their autonomy.
"But, it's pretty far out there at this point," he added.

Daley declined to comment on what legal action the city might take should the airport takeover bill become law. The Illinois Senate was expected to vote on the measure late Wednesday afternoon, according to Patty Schuh, spokeswoman for Senate President James "Pate" Philip, R-Wood Dale.
However, a coalition of park and open land groups was preparing a taxpayers lawsuit, according to officials at Daley's news conference.
Daley said if the state takes over Meigs Field, Illinois taxpayers would face paying $4 million for operating the airfield, as well as $30 million or more in capital expenses.
He also pointed out that the city has so far has come out the winner in lawsuits filed by the state in state and federal court in an attempt to block demolition of the airport.
"This is a 15 round title bout and we're in the first three rounds," he said, adding that there were "a lot of rounds to go."
